doc.title: Pug Horton interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 22, 1998

title: Upcoming plans for 1998
summary: She lists festivals, tours and a semi-retired year ahead with Bob.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: We need that. Well this has really been fascinating. What’s in the near future for you guys?

Well we leave for England on June the first. We go to Silkeborg in Denmark for a wonderful festival which is — now here’s the thing — sponsored by Tuborg Beer, which money is no object which is lovely so it shows you where their values are. But nonetheless, we’ve been going for three years now. We are going to be there with the Bechet legacy as I say with Phil Flanigan and Eddie Metz, Mark Shane and Dave Cliff, a wonderful guitarist from England that we’ve used a lot, and Eric Jon Kellso, the trumpet player. And then in July Bob is doing a mini-tour with Kenny Davern and we’re going to hang out in Juan-les-Pins, just to soak up the air as you would say and just enjoy it. And August we will be in France at festivals and in Toulouse. And then in September we’ve decided to go into France and look for a place that we thought we’d like to have a little place on the ocean in Normandy so we’re going to go and explore, and then we go to Japan with the Statesmen of Jazz, which is the one where Bob is the baby and the oldest member is 96. And then we do a big band cruise in November. And so it brings us to the end of 1998, and a year of semi-retirement.
That’s what I was about to say, my God.
But I have to tell you that, I mean not that Bob wants to hurt anyone’s feelings, but he turns down probably more work than many people are offered, because he wants to do © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-

the kind of things that he wants to do, and he’s doing it. And we’re both doing it and we’re enjoying it enormously. We have a very active life with our children and our grandchildren and so on, and next year looks like, with the exception of April when we will be in Paradise Valley and doing concerts in Denver and in Atlanta, I think that we have no work which is wonderful, just the month of April. And it pleases us because it gives us more time just to enjoy picking the grapefruit.
